voices.original_text: Can one AI model tackle harder work and still cost less to use?
voices.spoken_text: Can one AI model tackle harder work and still cost less to use?

voices.original_text: On September twenty-second, Anthropic announced Claude Opus five point five, the first model in its five point five family.
voices.spoken_text: On September twenty-second, Anthropic announced Claude Opus five point five, the first model in its five point five family.

voices.original_text: It’s built for long coding jobs and knowledge work: tasks where an AI can use tools, make several moves, and keep going toward a result.
voices.spoken_text: It’s built for long coding jobs and knowledge work: tasks where an AI can use tools, make several moves, and keep going toward a result.

voices.original_text: Anthropic reports gains on its tests for coding agents, computer use, and professional tasks. Those are company-reported benchmark results.
voices.spoken_text: Anthropic reports gains on its tests for coding agents, computer use, and professional tasks. Those are company-reported benchmark results.

voices.original_text: A benchmark is a set of test problems, not every messy job in the real world. A higher score cannot promise the same result for you.
voices.spoken_text: A benchmark is a set of test problems, not every messy job in the real world. A higher score cannot promise the same result for you.

voices.original_text: The bill counts tokens: small chunks of text going in and coming back out. Input is your side. Output is the model’s reply.
voices.spoken_text: The bill counts tokens: small chunks of text going in and coming back out. Input is your side. Output is the model’s reply.

voices.original_text: Opus five point five costs four dollars per million input tokens and twenty dollars per million output tokens. Anthropic estimates typical workloads cost forty percent less than Opus five at default settings. That saving isn’t promised on every request.
voices.spoken_text: Opus five point five costs four dollars per million input tokens and twenty dollars per million output tokens. Anthropic estimates typical workloads cost forty percent less than Opus five at default settings. That saving isn’t promised on every request.

voices.original_text: One outside check came from Artificial Analysis. At maximum effort, it scored Opus five point five fifty-eight on its own Intelligence Index, leading six of ten tests. That’s one independent scorecard, not a universal ranking.
voices.spoken_text: One outside check came from Artificial Analysis. At maximum effort, it scored Opus five point five fifty-eight on its own Intelligence Index, leading six of ten tests. That’s one independent scorecard, not a universal ranking.

voices.original_text: Sonar’s separate Java test found nearly the same pass rate as Opus five: about eighty-eight percent across five hundred forty-four tested tasks. Its bug rate per line went up, while some other code findings went down.
voices.spoken_text: Sonar’s separate Java test found nearly the same pass rate as Opus five: about eighty-eight percent across five hundred forty-four tested tasks. Its bug rate per line went up, while some other code findings went down.

voices.original_text: METR tested five difficult AI research tasks over ten business days. It judged the gain over Fable five point one modest, not full automation. Anthropic could review and edit the public summary; METR did not assess alignment or policy-threshold compliance.
voices.spoken_text: METR tested five difficult AI research tasks over ten business days. It judged the gain over Fable five point one modest, not full automation. Anthropic could review and edit the public summary; METR did not assess alignment or policy-threshold compliance.

voices.original_text: Artificial Analysis, Sonar, and METR each tested a narrow slice. Together, their launch-week findings don’t verify Anthropic’s full performance claims or its forty-percent typical-workload saving.
voices.spoken_text: Artificial Analysis, Sonar, and METR each tested a narrow slice. Together, their launch-week findings don’t verify Anthropic’s full performance claims or its forty-percent typical-workload saving.

voices.original_text: Anthropic says Opus five point five has powerful biology and cybersecurity abilities, so it adds classifiers and restrictions. High-risk dual-use cyber work is limited, but finding vulnerabilities in source code is allowed. Vetted life-science groups can apply.
voices.spoken_text: Anthropic says Opus five point five has powerful biology and cybersecurity abilities, so it adds classifiers and restrictions. High-risk dual-use cyber work is limited, but finding vulnerabilities in source code is allowed. Vetted life-science groups can apply.

voices.original_text: Verified cybersecurity practitioners can also apply as that program expands. These safeguards add barriers. They don’t make a powerful model risk-free.
voices.spoken_text: Verified cybersecurity practitioners can also apply as that program expands. These safeguards add barriers. They don’t make a powerful model risk-free.

voices.original_text: So the announcement is a trade-off to watch: stronger results on several tests, lower typical costs by Anthropic’s estimate, and extra gates where capabilities could be misused.
voices.spoken_text: So the announcement is a trade-off to watch: stronger results on several tests, lower typical costs by Anthropic’s estimate, and extra gates where capabilities could be misused.
